hook.text: eBay was the internet's marketplace. Then Amazon ate its lunch. eBay's GMV stagnated for a decade.

buildup.text: eBay relied on auctions while Amazon built fast shipping, reviews, and returns. Convenience trumped price.

discovery.text: Professional sellers preferred Amazon's managed services. eBay's hands-off approach became a weakness.

twist.text: eBay still makes $10 billion in revenue—it's profitable. It just stopped growing. Decline isn't always death.

climax.text: eBay's story shows that marketplace leadership requires constant reinvention. Standing still means falling behind.

punchline.text: Profitable but stagnant. eBay stopped innovating and the world moved on.

quiz.question: What caused eBay's stagnation?
options: Amazon offered superior convenience and managed services

details.summary: eBay pioneered consumer-to-consumer e-commerce with its auction model but declined as Amazon's fixed-price marketplace offered a faster, more reliable shopping experience..
details.whyItMatters: eBay's decline shows how an innovative marketplace model can become obsolete when user preferences shift. The auction format that made eBay unique became a friction point as consumers prioritized speed and certainty over discovery and deals.
takeaways: eBay's auction model lost relevance as consumers preferred fixed-price purchasing
Amazon's consistent buying experience with fast shipping outcompeted eBay's variety
Auction excitement mattered less when price comparison tools made bargains findable everywhere

faq.question: What caused eBay to lose market share to Amazon?
faq.answer: Amazon offered consistent product listings, reliable fulfillment, easy returns, and Prime shipping. eBay's variable seller quality, inconsistent shipping times, and auction bidding created uncertainty..

faq.question: Could eBay have adapted its model to compete with Amazon?
faq.answer: eBay did shift toward fixed-price listings and improved seller standards, but the transition was slow and incomplete. Its decentralized seller model made standardizing fulfillment quality difficult..
